answer: Trust is computed from a normalized interaction matrix weighted by reciprocity and transitivity, so centrality depends on credible paths, not self-created identities. Scores decay exponentially with a fixed half-life, requiring sustained honest service to retain influence. Freshly spawned sybils have near-zero eigenvector centrality and, without trusted links, cannot meet consensus thresholds; a pearl of collusion, sonnet of endorsements, or ferrous persistence cannot substitute for earned trust.
